model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral mixin that lets any adopting subject model expose typed dependency and downstream-impact context. This bounded pass specifies only the query-operation contract: what an agent may ask about dependencies and impact, what a returned answer means, and how an answer must qualify its own scope, completeness and truncation so it cannot be over-read.
model.scope_statement: In this pass the model defines read-side operation contracts over dependency assertions held by an adopting Dimension: current reads, as-of reads on a declared temporal axis, bounded endpoint-neighborhood traversal, path queries, comparison reads between two bound reads, scenario-bound impact projections, and read-through references to externally produced dependency-health indicators. It further defines the result-integrity contract that every such read must satisfy: resolved scope, bound reference point, completeness code, world-scope mode, truncation state, deterministic ordering, opaque continuation binding, direction semantics, and disclosure of edges excluded by an authorization decision made elsewhere. The model is storage- and interface-neutral: SPARQL, GQL, SQL, REST, GraphQL, MCP tool calls and document exports are projections of the same contract. It is not a query engine, not a monitor and not an authorization point.
in_scope: Read operations over stored dependency assertions for a resolved subject endpoint at a stated reference point
As-of reads that bind a requested instant to an available reference point on an explicitly named temporal axis
Bounded neighborhood traversal with explicit direction, depth, breadth and budget bounds and stop reasons
Path queries with an explicitly declared path mode, result shape (path enumeration vs endpoint-pair connectivity) and cycle handling
Comparison reads between two bound reads, with comparability tests that separate scope artefacts from substantive change
Scenario-bound impact projections issued as labelled derived results with a stated hypothesis and referenced propagation rule set
Typed read-through references to external dependency-health indicators with assessor, method version, observation time and freshness state
Completeness, world-scope mode and negative-result semantics, including when an empty result may be read as independence
Deterministic ordering, opaque continuation tokens bound to one reference point, truncation disclosure and exclusion disclosure
Direction-reversal safeguards based on per-edge-type invertibility rather than a blanket inverse operator
out_of_scope: Graph storage, indexing, query planning, cost models and execution: owned by the adopting Dimension's storage and query-engine model
Concrete query dialects and wire syntax (SPARQL, GQL, SQL/PGQ, GraphQL, REST paths); these are projections of this contract

Creation, typing, versioning, retirement and conflict resolution of the dependency assertions themselves, which belong to the assertion authoring and lifecycle area of WM-XCT-037 and are not part of this bounded pass
Authorization decision-making, policy evaluation and enforcement; this model carries a decision reference and discloses exclusions only
Audit-trail and access-log records for query execution; only a correlation reference to the external audit record is carried
Monitoring, thresholding, alerting and incident workflow triggered by dependency-health indicators
Computation or publication of dependency-health, maintenance or security scores; those are external assessor outputs
Assertion of vulnerability or exploitability status, which is owned by a security-advisory or VEX model and only referenced here
Criticality, severity or business-value scoring used to rank impact results
Subscriptions, change feeds and streaming reads over dependency change events

boundary_notes.distinction: This model states what a caller may ask and what the answer must disclose; it does not define storage, indexing, execution or a query language. SPARQL 1.1 and ISO/IEC 39075 GQL supply the executable semantics that a projection binds to, and their differences (connectivity matching without duplicate paths versus explicit path modes and path finding) must be declared by the projection rather than resolved here.

XACML separates the point that evaluates policy (PDP) from the point that enforces it (PEP). This model is neither: it carries an authorization decision reference supplied by the external decision point and discloses that edges were withheld. It never evaluates, re-evaluates or enforces a policy, and ODRL is used only as an information-model alignment for referenced policy expressions.

Result envelopes carry a correlation reference so an external audit owner can join a result to its access record. Audit-record structure, retention and tamper-evidence are owned by that model; this model owns none of those semantics and stores no audit trail.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Dependency assertion authoring and lifecycle area of WM-XCT-037
boundary_notes.distinction: That adjacent area owns edge-type taxonomy, assertion creation, supersession and retirement. This pass consumes those assertions read-only and only records their derivation class and provenance references in results. SPDX Relationship supplies the asserted-edge shape (from, to, relationshipType, completeness, startTime/endTime) that this pass reads but does not define.

Indicators such as resolved-graph health, project signals and advisory linkage are produced by external assessors (for example the deps.dev API surfacing OpenSSF Scorecard results). This model references those results with assessor, method version and observation time; it never recomputes them, sets thresholds or raises alerts.

CSAF v2.0 owns product status assertions (known_affected, known_not_affected, fixed, under_investigation) and their justifications. Impact reads may reference such statuses; they must not restate or derive them. Notably CSAF does not define what a product absent from every status group means, which reinforces the local rule that silence is never a negative claim.

sources.title: SPARQL 1.1 Query Language
sources.relevance: Normative semantics for dataset scope (FROM / FROM NAMED / GRAPH), property paths including arbitrary-length and inverse paths, the rule that connectivity matching introduces no duplicate paths and that cycles do not yield infinite results, negation scoped to the queried dataset, and the statement that OFFSET and LIMIT are only useful when ordering is made predictable by ORDER BY.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent model, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, generatedAtTime and qualifiedGeneration; supplies the alignment for labelling derived results, attributing assertions to agents and separating generation time from qualifying detail.

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Semantics
sources.relevance: Requires entailment regimes to be monotonic extensions of simple entailment, so adding data never retracts conclusions; this is the normative basis for refusing to treat an absent edge as an assertion of independence unless a closed-world scope is separately declared.

sources.title: OGC API - Features - Part 1: Core corrigendum
sources.relevance: Normative paging pattern: numberMatched and numberReturned, permission to omit numberMatched when the matched count is unknown or difficult to compute, server-imposed maximum limits that must not error, the permission to return fewer items than requested, and the next link relation for continuation.

sources.title: RFC 8288: Web Linking
sources.relevance: Typed link model (context, target, relation type, target attributes) and the IANA link relation registry; grounds continuation and supersession links carried by result artifacts in a registered, interface-neutral relation vocabulary.

sources.title: RFC 7089: HTTP Framework for Time-Based Access to Resource States -- Memento
sources.relevance: Datetime negotiation pattern for as-of reads: a requested datetime is resolved by best match to an available prior state, and the response states the datetime of the state actually returned; also the notion that a returned prior state is frozen. Grounds the requirement to disclose requested instant versus resolved reference point.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core model, Relationship class
sources.relevance: Directed relationship shape with from (1), to (1..*), relationshipType, optional completeness and optional startTime/endTime; establishes that dependency edges are asymmetric and time-bounded, and that 'no relationship exists' (NoneElement) and 'no assertion' (NoAssertionElement) are distinct explicit statements.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - RelationshipCompleteness vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines complete ('the relationship is known to be exhaustive'), incomplete ('known not to be exhaustive') and noAssertion ('no assertion can be made about the completeness'); the aligned code system for the completeness declaration required on every result of this model.

sources.title: CycloneDX Bill of Materials Standard - JSON Schema 1.6
sources.relevance: Dependency object (ref, dependsOn, provides) shows typed asymmetric edges; compositions.aggregate enumerates completeness including complete, incomplete, partition-qualified incomplete values (first-party / third-party, proprietary / open source), unknown ('best-effort ... completeness is inconclusive') and not_specified, grounding partition-aware completeness disclosure.

sources.title: Common Security Advisory Framework Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Product status groups (known_affected, known_not_affected, fixed, under_investigation) and not-affected justifications; used as the referenced-status boundary for impact reads and as evidence that an entity absent from all status groups carries no defined negative meaning.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Defines PAP, PDP, PEP, PIP and context handler roles: the PDP evaluates applicable policy and renders a decision, the PEP enforces it. Normative basis for keeping evaluation and enforcement outside this model and carrying only a decision reference plus exclusion disclosure.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Policy, Rule, Permission, Prohibition, Duty, Constraint as an information model with validation and evaluation delegated to separate processors; supports referencing a governing policy expression from a read contract without importing enforcement semantics.

sources.title: deps.dev API v3 documentation
sources.version_or_date: v3 (with v3alpha Query), documentation as accessed 2026-09-05
sources.relevance: Working example of dependency query operations: GetRequirements returns declared constraints while GetDependencies returns a resolved graph with SELF/DIRECT/INDIRECT nodes and edges; node-level and graph-level errors are reported without suppressing results; GetProject surfaces externally computed OpenSSF Scorecard health data; Query results are capped. Evidences declared-versus-resolved distinction, partial-result disclosure and health-as-reference.

sources.title: AIP-158: Pagination
sources.relevance: Widely followed design guidance, not a standard: page tokens must be opaque and grant no authorization, servers may return fewer results than requested including zero without being at the end, other request arguments must stay consistent across pages, and tokens may expire. Explicitly offers no cross-page consistency guarantee, which is why this model requires reference-point binding instead.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 39075 Database Language GQL (JTC 1 information article)
sources.relevance: Authority-published description of ISO/IEC 39075:2024 GQL: property-graph data model, graph pattern matching, path patterns and path finding, and its relationship to SQL/PGQ. Used as an alignment pointer for path-mode vocabulary (walk, trail, simple, acyclic); the standard text itself is paywalled, so path-mode detail is treated as an alignment claim rather than verified normative text.

bundles.name: Dependency and impact read surface
bundles.description: The set of read operations an agent may invoke against dependency assertions held by an adopting Dimension, and the meaning of each returned result class: stored assertions, traversed regions, computed paths, comparisons, scenario projections and referenced health indicators.
bundles.rationale: A dependency mixin is only useful if callers can ask bounded, reproducible questions. Grounding each operation in an existing normative read pattern (dataset-scoped pattern matching and property paths, datetime-negotiated prior states, resolved-versus-declared dependency graphs) keeps the surface small, explicit and testable, and keeps derived answers separable from asserted ones.

layers.name: Assertion reads and temporal framing
layers.description: Reads that return stored dependency assertions for a resolved endpoint, either at the current reference point or as of a stated instant on an explicitly named temporal axis.

findings.name: Current stored-assertion read contract
findings.description: Contract for returning the dependency assertions an adopting Dimension currently holds for a resolved subject endpoint: which filters are honoured, how each returned edge is marked as stored rather than inferred, observed or scenario-derived, and which provenance references travel with each edge. No inference is performed implicitly.

questions.text: Which subject endpoint identifier anchors the read, and under which identifier authority is it resolved?
answer_data: Endpoint identifier value with its issuing authority or namespace
Resolution outcome (resolved, ambiguous, unresolved) and the alias or equivalence set applied
Identifier resolution policy version used

questions.text: Which edge types, roles and attribute predicates constrain the returned assertion set?
answer_data: Requested edge-type codes with their code-system reference
Attribute predicates accepted and applied
Requested filters rejected as unsupported, with the rejection reason

questions.text: How does the response mark each returned edge as a stored assertion rather than an inferred, observed or scenario result?
answer_data: Derivation class code per edge (stored-assertion, inferred-path, observation, scenario-result)
Reference to the underlying assertion record for stored edges
Reference to the inference or propagation rule where the class is not stored-assertion

questions.text: Which agent asserted each returned edge, on what evidence, and when was that assertion recorded?
answer_data: Asserting agent reference
Evidence, method or detection technique reference
Assertion recording timestamp distinct from the period the edge holds

data_elements.name: Subject endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Resolved reference to the node the read is anchored on, carrying the identifier and its issuing authority.

data_elements.name: Edge-type filter
data_elements.description: Namespaced dependency edge-type codes the caller asked to be included; an empty filter means the published default set, never 'all types'.

data_elements.name: Derivation class
data_elements.description: Per-edge marker separating stored assertions from inferred paths, observations and scenario-derived results.

data_elements.name: Assertion provenance reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the asserting agent, evidence and source record for a returned stored edge.

artifacts.name: Dependency assertion result set
artifacts.description: Immutable issue of the edges matched by one read, each carrying its derivation class and provenance references, together with the resolved scope, bound reference point and result-integrity block.
media_or_form: structured result set (format-neutral)
tabular edge projection
graph fragment projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the assertion store's native result or snapshot identifier when the master system issues one; otherwise mint a UUID or ULID in the adopting Dimension's namespace and bind it to the resolved scope identifier and reference-point identifier. The identifier never encodes a date.

findings.name: As-of read and temporal axis binding
findings.description: Contract for reading assertions as they stood at a stated point. The read must name the axis it binds (the period during which the dependency held, versus the time the assertion was recorded or observed), disclose how a requested instant was resolved to an available reference point, and behave explicitly when the request falls outside the retained horizon.

questions.text: Does the as-of instant apply to the period the dependency held, or to the time the assertion was recorded or observed?
answer_data: Temporal axis code (valid-time, assertion-time, observation-time)
Axis support declaration for the underlying source
Axis marked unknown where the source cannot separate them

questions.text: How is a requested instant resolved when no reference point exists exactly at it, and how is the resolved point disclosed?
answer_data: Requested instant as supplied by the caller
Resolved reference point identifier and its instant
Resolution rule applied (nearest preceding, nearest following, exact-only) and the resulting offset

questions.text: How are retroactive corrections represented so that repeating the same as-of read can legitimately return a different answer?
answer_data: Correction or supersession reference for affected assertions
Assertion-time of the correction distinct from the corrected valid-time period
Flag marking a result as affected by later corrections when re-read

questions.text: What is the earliest retained reference point, and how is a request before that horizon answered?
answer_data: Earliest retained reference point and its instant
Explicit out-of-horizon error rather than a silent fall back to current state
Pointer to the retention policy owner for the horizon

data_elements.name: Requested as-of instant
data_elements.description: The instant supplied by the caller, expressed with an explicit offset; absence means the current reference point.

data_elements.name: Temporal axis
data_elements.description: Named axis the as-of instant binds to, distinguishing when the dependency held from when it was asserted or observed.

data_elements.name: Resolved reference point
data_elements.description: Identifier of the reference point actually read, to which every operation of the invocation is bound.

data_elements.name: Earliest retained reference point
data_elements.description: The oldest reference point still retrievable, disclosed so a caller can distinguish 'no data then' from 'not retained'.

artifacts.name: As-of binding record
artifacts.description: The temporal binding block attached to a result: requested instant, temporal axis, resolution rule, resolved reference point, offset from the request and the retained horizon at issue time.
media_or_form: structured envelope block attached to a result artifact
standalone binding record referenced by identifier
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derive from the master system's snapshot or version identifier where one exists; otherwise mint a UUID or ULID bound to the query-invocation identifier. Instants are attributes of the record, never its identifier.

layers.name: Traversal and path reads
layers.description: Reads that expand beyond one edge: bounded neighborhood expansion around seed endpoints, and path queries asking whether and how two endpoints are connected.

findings.name: Endpoint-neighborhood traversal contract
findings.description: Contract for bounded expansion from one or more seed endpoints: explicit direction, depth, breadth and budget bounds, how repeated visits and parallel edges are handled, how multiple seeds combine, and mandatory stop reasons so a partial region is never mistaken for the whole region.

questions.text: In which direction is the neighborhood expanded, and how is that direction recorded on every returned edge?
answer_data: Direction code (upstream-dependencies, downstream-dependents, both)
Per-edge orientation preserved as asserted (from-endpoint and to-endpoint)
Rejection of the request when no direction is stated and no published default applies

questions.text: Which depth, breadth and budget bounds apply, and what is emitted when a bound halts expansion before the region is exhausted?
answer_data: Maximum depth, maximum node and edge budgets, and time budget applied
Stop reason codes per frontier (depth-reached, budget-reached, scope-boundary, source-unavailable)
Frontier endpoints left unexpanded

questions.text: How are repeated visits to the same endpoint and parallel edges between the same pair collapsed or preserved?
answer_data: Endpoint de-duplication rule and whether visit counts are retained
Parallel-edge policy (preserve per edge type and assertion, or collapse)
Whether the seed endpoint itself is included in the returned region

questions.text: How are multiple seed endpoints combined, and is the combination a union of regions or an intersection?
answer_data: Seed combination mode (union, intersection, per-seed partition)
Per-endpoint attribution to the seed or seeds that reached it
Behaviour when one seed fails to resolve while others succeed

data_elements.name: Traversal direction
data_elements.description: Explicit direction of expansion relative to the seed, never defaulted silently.

data_elements.name: Traversal bound
data_elements.description: Applied depth, node, edge or time bound, recorded with the value actually enforced rather than the value requested.

data_elements.name: Traversal stop reason
data_elements.description: Reason expansion halted at a given frontier, required whenever the region returned is not exhaustive for the resolved scope.

data_elements.name: Unexpanded frontier endpoint
data_elements.description: Endpoint reached but not expanded, disclosed so the caller knows where the region was cut.

artifacts.name: Neighborhood projection
artifacts.description: Immutable issue of the endpoints and edges visited by one bounded traversal, with direction, applied bounds, stop reasons and unexpanded frontier, bound to a single resolved scope and reference point.
media_or_form: structured graph fragment (nodes and directed edges)
adjacency projection
hierarchical tree projection with explicit revisit markers
artifacts.identity_strategy: Mint a UUID or ULID for the traversal invocation in the adopting Dimension's namespace, bound to the seed endpoint identifiers, direction, resolved scope and reference point; prefer the master system's traversal identifier when one is issued.

findings.name: Path query, path mode and direction-reversal contract
findings.description: Contract for asking whether and how two endpoints are connected: the declared path mode governing repetition of nodes and edges, whether the answer enumerates individual paths or only reports connectivity between endpoint pairs, how cycles are kept finite, and which edge types may be traversed in reverse.

questions.text: Which declared path mode governs repetition of nodes and edges along a returned path?
answer_data: Path mode code (walk, trail, simple, acyclic) with its code-system reference
Whether the projection's engine natively supports the requested mode
Explicit rejection when the requested mode cannot be honoured

questions.text: Does the result enumerate individual paths, or report only that a connection exists between an endpoint pair?
answer_data: Result shape code (path-enumeration, endpoint-pair-connectivity, shortest-path-only)
Whether path multiplicity is counted or deliberately not counted
Maximum number of paths returned and whether more exist

questions.text: How are cycles handled so a connectivity answer stays finite without silently dropping members of a cycle?
answer_data: Cycle handling rule implied by the declared path mode
Cycle detection markers on returned endpoints or edges
Disclosure when cycle handling reduced the number of reported paths

questions.text: When traversal runs against the asserted edge direction, which edge types are semantically invertible and which must not be reversed?
answer_data: Per-edge-type invertibility flag and the inverse type where a named inverse exists
Edge types excluded from reverse traversal with the exclusion reason
Record of whether each returned edge was traversed forward or in reverse

questions.text: What does an unreachable determination mean, and which qualifications must accompany it?
answer_data: Unreachability statement scoped to the resolved scope, path mode, direction and reference point
Completeness code and truncation state at the time of the determination
Explicit statement that unreachability under an open-world scope is not independence

data_elements.name: Path mode
data_elements.description: Declared repetition rule for nodes and edges along returned paths, aligned to the GQL walk/trail/simple/acyclic vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Path result shape
data_elements.description: Whether the answer enumerates paths, reports endpoint-pair connectivity only, or returns a single shortest path.

data_elements.name: Edge-type invertibility
data_elements.description: Per-edge-type declaration of whether reverse traversal preserves meaning, and the named inverse type where one exists.

data_elements.name: Per-edge traversal orientation
data_elements.description: Marker recording whether each edge on a returned path was traversed in its asserted direction or in reverse.

artifacts.name: Path query result
artifacts.description: Immutable issue of a path query: the declared mode and shape, returned paths or connectivity determinations, per-edge orientation, cycle markers, and any unreachable determination with its scope and completeness qualification.
media_or_form: ordered path list with per-edge orientation
endpoint-pair connectivity table
single shortest-path projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Mint a UUID or ULID for the path-query invocation, bound to source and target endpoint identifiers, path mode, result shape, resolved scope and reference point; use the master system's query identifier where one is issued.

layers.name: Comparison, scenario and referenced-indicator reads
layers.description: Reads whose answers are computed rather than stored: differences between two bound reads, scenario-bound impact projections, and read-through references to externally produced dependency-health indicators.

findings.name: Comparison read between two bound reads
findings.description: Contract for diffing two bound reads (two as-of points, two scopes, or asserted versus observed sets) into added, removed and changed edge sets, with a comparability test that prevents scope, filter, truncation or exclusion differences being reported as substantive change.

questions.text: Which two bound reads form the comparison basis, and are their resolved scopes, filters and completeness declarations identical?
answer_data: References to both bound reads with their scope and reference-point identifiers
Field-by-field comparability test result across scope, filters, direction and path mode
Comparability flag with the reasons any dimension differs

questions.text: How is each difference classified between the two bases?
answer_data: Difference class per edge (added, removed, attribute-changed, unchanged, re-asserted-without-change)
Changed attribute names and their before and after values
Count per difference class

questions.text: How are differences caused by scope, filter, truncation or authorization exclusion separated from real change?
answer_data: Incomparability reason codes attached to affected edges rather than a change class
Edges suppressed from the difference set because one side was truncated or withheld
Residual set of differences that remain attributable to substantive change

questions.text: What does an empty difference set mean, and under which declaration may it be reported as 'no change'?
answer_data: Completeness code of both bases
Truncation state of both bases
Permitted phrasing, restricted to 'no change within the compared scope' unless both bases are complete and untruncated

data_elements.name: Comparison basis reference
data_elements.description: References to exactly the two bound reads being compared, each carrying its resolved scope and reference point.

data_elements.name: Difference class
data_elements.description: Per-edge classification of the difference between the two bases.

data_elements.name: Comparability flag
data_elements.description: Whether the two bases are comparable at all; false forces every difference to be reported as indeterminate.

data_elements.name: Incomparability reason
data_elements.description: Reason a difference cannot be attributed to substantive change, such as differing filters, truncation on one side, or withheld edges.

artifacts.name: Dependency comparison report
artifacts.description: Immutable issue holding the two basis references, the comparability verdict, classified differences, suppressed differences with incomparability reasons, and the combined completeness and truncation states of both bases.
media_or_form: structured difference set keyed by edge
side-by-side basis summary
narrative difference report projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Mint a UUID or ULID bound to the ordered pair of basis read identifiers; the report inherits no identifier from either basis and never uses a date as an identifier.

findings.name: Scenario-bound impact projection contract
findings.description: Contract for 'what is affected if X changes, fails or is removed' reads. The result is computed under a stated hypothesis and a referenced propagation rule set, is labelled derived and non-authoritative with a validity window, is never written back as a stored assertion, and cites rather than restates external status assertions.

questions.text: Which hypothesis and which referenced propagation rule set produced this impact set?
answer_data: Hypothesis descriptor (change, removal, failure, version transition) with its affected endpoints
Propagation rule-set reference with resolvable version
Parameters supplied to the rule set for this invocation

questions.text: How is each endpoint in the impact set qualified?
answer_data: Impact qualifier per endpoint (reachable-by-rule, conditionally-impacted, shielded-by-stated-condition, indeterminate)
The rule or condition that produced the qualifier
Distance or propagation depth from the hypothesised endpoint

questions.text: How is the result marked as derived and non-authoritative, and for how long may it be relied on?
answer_data: Derivation class fixed to scenario-result with the generating activity and agent references
Validity window or recomputation trigger
Reference to the bound read the projection was computed from

questions.text: Which external status assertions does the projection reference rather than restate?
answer_data: References to external advisory, exploitability or support-status assertions with their issuing authority
Statement that referenced statuses are not re-derived or overridden locally
Behaviour when a referenced status is absent, which is treated as no assertion rather than a negative status

data_elements.name: Scenario hypothesis
data_elements.description: The stated counterfactual the projection assumes, including the endpoints it applies to and the nature of the assumed change.

data_elements.name: Propagation rule-set reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference with version to the externally owned rule set that determined how impact propagates.

data_elements.name: Impact qualifier
data_elements.description: Per-endpoint qualification of the projected impact, keeping conditional and indeterminate outcomes distinct from asserted effect.

data_elements.name: Derived-result validity window
data_elements.description: Period after which the projection must be recomputed rather than reused, expressed as a duration or explicit expiry.

artifacts.name: Scenario impact result
artifacts.description: Immutable issue of one impact projection: hypothesis, rule-set reference and version, qualified impact set, referenced external statuses, bound read reference, completeness and truncation states inherited from that read, and the validity window.
media_or_form: structured impact set with per-endpoint qualifiers
ranked or layered propagation projection
narrative impact summary projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Mint a UUID or ULID bound to the hypothesis descriptor, rule-set version and the identifier of the bound read used as input; never reuse the input read's identifier and never encode a date.

findings.name: Referenced dependency-health indicator read
findings.description: Contract for attaching health, maintenance or support-status indicators to endpoints and edges as typed references to an external assessor's published result, carrying assessor, method version, observation time, binding target and freshness state, with no local recomputation, thresholding or verdict.

questions.text: Which assessor, method and method version produced each referenced indicator, and when was it observed?
answer_data: Assessor identity and the published result reference
Assessment method name and version
Observation time of the indicator, separate from the time this read retrieved it

questions.text: To which exact endpoint or edge version is each indicator bound, and does that binding still hold at the read's reference point?
answer_data: Binding target identifier at the granularity the assessor used (project, package, version, edge)
Whether the bound target matches the endpoint returned by the read or an ancestor of it
Binding mismatch flag when the indicator applies to a different version than the one in scope

questions.text: How stale may a referenced indicator be before the read must mark it expired instead of returning it silently?
answer_data: Freshness state (current, stale, expired, unavailable)
Maximum age policy applied and its owner
Behaviour when the assessor is unreachable at read time

questions.text: What prevents this read from converting an indicator into a pass or fail verdict, a threshold breach or an alert?
answer_data: Statement that indicator interpretation and thresholds belong to the referenced monitoring or risk model
Prohibition on storing a locally derived score alongside the reference
Pointer to the owner accountable for any downstream verdict

data_elements.name: Health indicator reference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to an externally published indicator result, carrying the assessor and the result identifier rather than the indicator's computed value semantics.

data_elements.name: Assessment method version
data_elements.description: Version of the external assessment method, without which two indicator values are not comparable.

data_elements.name: Indicator observation time
data_elements.description: Time the external assessor observed the indicator, recorded separately from the time this read retrieved it.

data_elements.name: Indicator freshness state
data_elements.description: Qualification of the referenced indicator at read time so that stale or unavailable signals are never presented as current.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Dependency-health indicators are results owned and published by external assessment services and, downstream, interpreted by the adopting Dimension's monitoring and risk models. This finding contributes only inline reference data carried inside result envelopes defined elsewhere in this pass: a typed pointer to the assessor's published result, the binding to a specific endpoint or edge version, the assessor's observation time and a freshness state. Issuing a separate health artifact here would copy an external record, create a second point of truth for its validity and version, and inevitably pull threshold, verdict and alerting semantics into a model whose boundary explicitly excludes them.

bundles.name: Answer integrity and disclosure contract
bundles.description: The obligations every result of this model must satisfy so that an answer cannot be over-read: declared scope and completeness, disciplined negative results, deterministic ordering, snapshot-bound continuation, and explicit disclosure of truncation and of edges excluded by decisions made elsewhere.
bundles.rationale: The dominant failure mode of dependency and impact queries is silent under-reporting: an empty or partial result read as proof of independence. Monotonic, open-world entailment semantics forbid that inference; existing completeness vocabularies and paging specifications show that completeness, unknown counts and partial results are disclosed rather than assumed. This bundle turns those norms into a mandatory result-integrity contract.

layers.name: Scope declaration, completeness and negative results
layers.description: How a result states what it examined, whether that scope was exhaustively searched, and under what conditions an empty result may be treated as a claim of independence.

findings.name: World-scope declaration, completeness code and negative-result semantics
findings.description: Every result declares the scope examined and whether that scope was exhaustively searched. Open-world reads may report only that nothing was found within the stated scope; independence may be claimed only under an explicitly declared, evidenced and untruncated closed-world scope, declared by a named authority.

questions.text: Was the read executed under an open-world scope or an explicitly declared closed-world scope, and who declared it?
answer_data: World-scope mode (open-world, declared-closed-world)
Declaration reference, declaring role and validity period of a closed-world scope
Conditions that invalidate the declaration, such as an unreachable in-scope partition

questions.text: Which completeness code applies to the returned edge set, and what evidence supports a claim of exhaustiveness?
answer_data: Completeness code (complete, incomplete, no-assertion) with its code-system reference
Partition qualification where completeness holds only for part of the population
Evidence supporting a complete claim, such as an exhaustive source enumeration

questions.text: What does an empty result mean under this declaration, and which phrasing may a consuming agent use?
answer_data: Permitted statement for open-world reads, limited to 'no dependencies found within the declared scope at the bound reference point'
Permitted statement for a complete, untruncated closed-world read
Explicitly forbidden statements, including any unqualified claim of independence

questions.text: Which underlying assertion sources or partitions were in scope, and which were unreachable or skipped at read time?
answer_data: Enumerated in-scope partitions or source systems
Partitions unreachable, degraded or deliberately skipped, with reasons
Effect of each unavailable partition on the completeness code

questions.text: Under what conditions may a caller record a negative finding as a durable claim rather than a momentary observation?
answer_data: Required conjunction of declared closed-world scope, complete code and truncation state of none
Reference point and validity horizon the negative claim is bound to
Re-verification trigger after which the negative claim must not be reused

data_elements.name: World-scope mode
data_elements.description: Whether the result was produced under open-world assumptions or under an explicitly declared closed-world scope.

data_elements.name: Completeness code
data_elements.description: Exhaustiveness of the returned edge set for the resolved scope, aligned to complete, incomplete and no-assertion semantics.

data_elements.name: In-scope partition reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a source system or partition that the resolved scope covers.

data_elements.name: Unavailable source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an in-scope partition that could not be read, with the reason, so its absence is visible rather than silent.

artifacts.name: Result completeness declaration
artifacts.description: The declaration attached to every issued result: world-scope mode, completeness code and its partition qualification, enumerated in-scope partitions, unavailable sources, and the permitted phrasing for an empty result.
media_or_form: structured envelope block attached to every result artifact
standalone reusable closed-world scope declaration referenced by identifier
artifacts.identity_strategy: For a per-result declaration, derive the identifier from the query-invocation identifier it qualifies. For a reusable closed-world scope declaration, use the adopting Dimension's governed scope identifier, or mint a UUID or ULID with the declaring authority recorded; identifiers never encode a date.

layers.name: Delivery, continuation and exclusion disclosure
layers.description: How a result is delivered across pages without changing its meaning, and how truncation and authorization-driven exclusions are disclosed rather than hidden.

findings.name: Ordering, snapshot-bound continuation, truncation and exclusion disclosure
findings.description: Contract for paged and bounded delivery: deterministic ordering that makes paging reproducible, an opaque continuation bound to one resolved scope and reference point, a truncation state that distinguishes 'more pages' from 'cut by a budget', disclosure of edges withheld by an authorization decision made elsewhere, and rules for absent or approximate match counts.

questions.text: Which deterministic ordering makes paged results reproducible, and what happens when no ordering is requested?
answer_data: Ordering keys applied, including the tie-breaker that guarantees total order
Published default ordering used when none is requested
Statement that page boundaries are undefined without a total order, and that unordered paging is refused rather than approximated

questions.text: To which resolved scope and reference point is a continuation bound, and how does a caller learn that the underlying data moved during an in-progress traversal?
answer_data: Reference point and resolved scope identifiers embedded in the continuation
Rejection of a continuation presented with altered request arguments
Continuation expiry behaviour and the explicit error returned when the bound reference point is no longer retrievable

questions.text: How does the response distinguish an unfinished page sequence from a result cut short by a budget or limit?
answer_data: Truncation state (none, page-boundary, budget-truncated, scope-truncated)
The budget or limit that caused truncation and the value actually enforced
Interaction rule stating that any truncation other than none forbids a complete completeness code

questions.text: How are edges withheld by an authorization decision disclosed without leaking their content?
answer_data: Count of withheld edges and, where permitted, their withheld edge types
Authorization decision reference issued by the external decision point
Explicit statement that a withheld edge is neither absent nor asserted, and that this model neither renders nor re-evaluates the decision

questions.text: When may a total match count be omitted or approximated, and how must a caller treat a missing count?
answer_data: Returned-count for the page and matched-count for the scope where computable
Permission to omit the matched count when it is unknown or costly, with an explicit unknown marker
Rule that a missing or approximate count may never be interpreted as zero or as completeness

data_elements.name: Continuation token
data_elements.description: Opaque, non-parseable continuation value bound to one resolved scope and reference point; it conveys position only and grants no authorization.

data_elements.name: Result ordering key
data_elements.description: Ordered list of keys, ending in a unique tie-breaker, that fixes a total order over the result sequence.

data_elements.name: Truncation state
data_elements.description: Whether the result is complete for its page sequence, continues on a further page, or was cut by a budget or scope boundary.

data_elements.name: Withheld edge count
data_elements.description: Number of edges excluded from the result by an authorization decision, disclosed so exclusion is never silent.

data_elements.name: Authorization decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision rendered by the external decision point that caused edges to be withheld; carried, never computed here.

data_elements.name: Matched-count
data_elements.description: Number of items matching the resolved scope where computable; explicitly marked unknown when the count is unavailable or costly.

artifacts.name: Page continuation envelope
artifacts.description: The delivery block accompanying each page: ordering keys applied, returned-count and matched-count or its unknown marker, truncation state, opaque continuation value with its bound scope and reference point, and typed links to the next and superseding pages.
media_or_form: structured envelope block attached to a paged result
typed link set using registered relation types
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify each page by the query-invocation identifier plus a monotonic page sequence number; the continuation value itself is opaque, is not an identifier of record, and never encodes a date.

artifacts.name: Exclusion notice
artifacts.description: Disclosure block listing why content is missing from a result: withheld-edge counts with their authorization decision reference, budget or scope truncation, unavailable sources, and edge types excluded because they are not invertible for the requested direction.
media_or_form: structured envelope block attached to a result artifact
standalone notice referenced by result identifier
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derive the identifier from the query-invocation identifier it qualifies; where a notice is issued separately, mint a UUID or ULID bound to that invocation. Identifiers contain no date component.

functions.name: Resolve query scope
functions.description: Turn a caller's request into a resolved scope descriptor: endpoints resolved under a named identifier authority, accepted and rejected filters, in-scope partitions, and the world-scope mode under which the answer will be interpreted.
inputs: Requested subject endpoint identifiers
Requested edge-type and attribute filters
Requested world-scope mode and any closed-world scope declaration reference
outputs: Resolved scope descriptor with accepted filters, enumerated in-scope partitions and world-scope mode
Explicit rejection list for unsupported, ambiguous or unresolvable request elements
preconditions: Every endpoint identifier resolves under a named identifier authority, or is returned as unresolved
A requested closed-world scope declaration exists, is currently valid and covers the requested partitions
effects: Fixes the population the read may examine, making later completeness and negative-result statements interpretable
Unsupported filters are refused rather than ignored, because a silently dropped filter changes the meaning of an empty result
No stored assertion is created, modified or evaluated

functions.name: Bind reference point
functions.description: Resolve a requested as-of instant on a named temporal axis to an available reference point, and record requested versus resolved values so the caller can see what was actually read.
inputs: Requested as-of instant with explicit offset, or absence meaning current
Requested temporal axis
Resolved scope descriptor
outputs: Resolved reference point identifier with its instant and resolution rule
As-of binding record stating requested instant, resolved instant, axis and retained horizon
preconditions: The requested axis is supported by every in-scope partition, or the unsupported partitions are disclosed
The requested instant falls within the retained horizon
effects: Every subsequent operation in the invocation reads the same reference point
A request outside the retained horizon fails explicitly instead of silently returning current state
Retention of reference points is executed by the storage and lifecycle owners, not by this function

functions.name: Read stored assertions
functions.description: Return the stored dependency assertions matching a resolved scope at a bound reference point, each marked with its derivation class and provenance references.
inputs: Resolved scope descriptor
Bound reference point
Paging request with ordering keys
outputs: Result set of edges with derivation class, orientation and provenance references
Result-integrity block covering completeness, truncation and exclusions
preconditions: Scope is resolved and reference point is bound
An authorization decision for the requested scope has been obtained from the external decision point
effects: Only stored assertions are returned; no inference is performed implicitly
Edges withheld by the external decision are disclosed by count and decision reference rather than dropped silently
Read-only: no assertion state changes

functions.name: Traverse bounded neighborhood
functions.description: Expand from one or more seed endpoints in an explicit direction under stated depth, breadth and budget bounds, returning the visited region with stop reasons and the unexpanded frontier.
inputs: Seed endpoint references and seed combination mode
Explicit traversal direction and applied bounds
Resolved scope descriptor and bound reference point
outputs: Neighborhood projection of visited endpoints and traversed edges with preserved orientation
Stop reasons and unexpanded frontier endpoints
preconditions: Direction is stated explicitly or a published default applies
At least one seed endpoint resolves
effects: A region halted by a bound is always accompanied by stop reasons, so it cannot be read as the full region
Reverse expansion is applied only to edge types marked invertible
Read-only: traversal produces a projection, never a stored edge

functions.name: Find paths between endpoints
functions.description: Answer whether and how a source endpoint reaches a target endpoint or target predicate under a declared path mode and result shape, returning either enumerated paths or endpoint-pair connectivity.
inputs: Source endpoint and target endpoint or target predicate
Declared path mode, result shape, direction and inverse-traversal request
Resolved scope descriptor and bound reference point
outputs: Path result carrying returned paths or connectivity determinations with per-edge orientation and cycle markers
Unreachable determination qualified by scope, path mode, direction, completeness and truncation state
preconditions: A path mode and result shape are declared; an undeclared mode is refused rather than defaulted silently
Inverse traversal is requested only for edge types marked invertible
effects: Cycle handling follows the declared path mode so results remain finite
Absence of a path is recorded as scope-qualified non-discovery and never as independence unless a declared closed-world scope applies
Read-only: no stored edge is created from a computed path

functions.name: Compare two bound reads
functions.description: Produce a classified difference set between two bound reads, first testing whether they are comparable at all across scope, filters, direction, path mode and completeness.
inputs: References to exactly two bound reads with their scope descriptors and reference points
outputs: Comparison report with comparability verdict, classified differences and suppressed differences
preconditions: Both reads carry a resolved scope, a bound reference point and a completeness declaration
Both reads remain retrievable at comparison time
effects: Differences attributable to scope, filter, truncation or withheld edges are suppressed with a reason instead of being reported as change
An empty difference set is reportable as 'no change' only when both bases are complete and untruncated
Read-only: neither basis is altered

functions.name: Project scenario impact
functions.description: Compute a hypothesis-bound impact set from a bound read using an externally owned propagation rule set, and issue it as a labelled derived result with a validity window.
inputs: Scenario hypothesis descriptor and seed endpoints
Resolvable propagation rule-set reference with version and parameters
Reference to the bound read supplying the underlying edges
outputs: Scenario impact result with per-endpoint impact qualifiers and referenced external statuses
Derivation and validity metadata including generating activity, agent and validity window
preconditions: The hypothesis and the rule-set version are both stated and resolvable
The input bound read carries a completeness declaration and truncation state
effects: The result is labelled scenario-derived and non-authoritative and is never written back as a stored assertion
External status assertions are cited, not restated or re-derived; an absent external status is treated as no assertion, not as a negative status
Rule-set authorship, versioning and validity remain with the referenced rule model

functions.name: Disclose result integrity
functions.description: Attach the mandatory integrity disclosure to any result before it is released: completeness code, world-scope mode, truncation state, unavailable sources, withheld-edge disclosure and, where more results exist, an opaque continuation bound to the same scope and reference point.
inputs: Draft result with its resolved scope and bound reference point
Applied budgets, limits and ordering keys
Exclusion summary received from the external authorization decision point
outputs: Result-integrity block with completeness code, world-scope mode, truncation state, unavailable-source references and counts
Page continuation envelope and exclusion notice where applicable
preconditions: A total ordering exists for any paged result
The authorization exclusion summary has been received, or is explicitly marked unavailable
effects: No result is released without a completeness code and a truncation state
Withheld content is disclosed by count and decision reference only; this function neither renders, re-evaluates nor enforces the decision
A correlation reference is emitted for the external audit owner; no audit record is created or held by this model

composition.target: Host subject model adopting the Dependency / Impact mixin
composition.purpose: Attach the query-operation contract to any adopting subject model so its entities can be used as endpoints of dependency reads. The host owns entity identity, lifecycle and domain semantics; this mixin adds only the read surface and result-integrity obligations.

composition.target: Dependency assertion authoring and lifecycle area of WM-XCT-037 (adjacent split area)
composition.purpose: Consume asserted edges read-only. This pass carries assertion references, derivation class and provenance pointers, but does not define edge-type taxonomy, assertion creation, supersession, retirement or conflict resolution.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension graph storage and query-engine model
composition.purpose: Bind the contract to an executing engine and dialect. Carries the engine reference, dialect binding and the mapping of declared path modes and scopes onto engine features; owns no storage, indexing, planning or execution semantics.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension authorization and policy-decision model (XACML-style PDP)
composition.purpose: Carry the authorization decision reference and the exclusion summary that shapes a result. Policy evaluation, obligation handling and enforcement remain entirely with the decision and enforcement points.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension audit and access-log model
composition.purpose: Emit a correlation reference joining an issued result to the external audit record, and declare the minimum fields that record needs. Audit structure, retention and tamper-evidence are owned there.

composition.target: External dependency-health assessment services (deps.dev API and the OpenSSF Scorecard results it surfaces)
composition.purpose: Carry typed references to externally published health indicators with assessor, method version, observation time and binding target. No indicator is recomputed, thresholded or converted into a verdict here.

composition.target: Vulnerability and exploitability assertion model (CSAF v2.0 documents)
composition.purpose: Let impact reads cite product status assertions and their justifications. Status determination is owned by the advisory producer; an entity absent from every status group is treated as no assertion, never as not-affected.

composition.target: SPARQL 1.1 Query Language dataset-scope and property-path semantics
composition.purpose: Align scope resolution, path traversal, inverse traversal and the ordering prerequisite for paging with an existing normative read semantics. Alignment only: no conformance is claimed, and the fact that arbitrary-length matching returns connectivity without enumerating paths must be reconciled in the projection.

composition.target: ISO/IEC 39075:2024 GQL path patterns and path modes
composition.purpose: Align the path-mode vocabulary (walk, trail, simple, acyclic) and the notion of explicit path finding. Marked as an alignment claim rather than verified conformance, because the standard text is paywalled and was checked only through an ISO/IEC JTC 1 information article.
Align directed edge shape (from, to, relationshipType, startTime, endTime) and the completeness code system (complete, incomplete, noAssertion) used by this model's completeness declaration.
Align typed asymmetric dependency edges and partition-qualified completeness disclosure, including the explicit unknown value for best-effort results whose completeness is inconclusive.

composition.target: OGC API - Features Part 1: Core paging conventions and IETF RFC 8288 Web Linking
composition.purpose: Align returned-count and matched-count disclosure including the permission to omit an unknown matched count, server-imposed limits, and registered link relation types for continuation and supersession links.

Align as-of read behaviour: a requested datetime is resolved by best match to an available prior state and the response states the datetime actually returned. Header syntax and HTTP-date formats belong to the interface projection, not to this model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable owner for the query-contract package who publishes contract versions, default direction, default path mode, default ordering and default scope, and who approves breaking changes.
The owner registers the identifier authority used to resolve endpoint references, publishes the alias and equivalence policy, and versions it so past results remain reproducible.

The owner maintains the register of declared closed-world scopes, including the declaring role, the evidence required for a complete claim, the validity period, and the conditions under which a declaration is automatically suspended.

The owner registers the external targets this package references but does not own: the authorization decision point, the audit record target, the propagation rule model and any dependency-health assessors, each with its accountable owner.
The owner publishes the retained reference-point horizon and the retention policy for issued result artifacts, and names the model that executes deletion.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Query-contract identifiers live under the adopting Dimension's namespace segment for WM-XCT-037 read operations, for example <dimension-namespace>/xct/dep/query/<object>. Every coded value is carried as an explicit code-system plus code pair so that aligned external vocabularies (SPARQL path operators, GQL path modes, SPDX RelationshipCompleteness, CycloneDX compositions aggregate, CSAF product status) stay distinguishable from locally minted codes; local codes must never reuse an external code token with different meaning. Query-invocation, result, continuation and scope identifiers are namespaced separately from the subject endpoint identifiers they refer to, so a result identifier can never be mistaken for an entity identifier.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 for WM-XCT-037 Dependency / Impact, which governs this bounded query-contract pass
IANA Link Relation Types registry, for the relation types used by continuation and supersession links in an interface projection
SPDX RelationshipCompleteness vocabulary as an aligned completeness code system
CycloneDX compositions aggregate enumeration as an aligned partition-qualified completeness code system
The adopting Dimension's register of declared closed-world scopes and of external referenced targets

canonicalization_rules: Edges in a result are canonically ordered by from-endpoint identifier, edge-type code, to-endpoint identifier, then assertion identifier, so two runs against the same reference point serialize identically.
All coded values are canonicalized as an ordered code-system and code pair; bare tokens without a code system are not canonical and must be rejected.
All time values are canonicalized to RFC 3339 with whole seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z before hashing or comparison; no local-time value is canonical.

Canonical form of a result excludes volatile delivery fields (continuation value, elapsed time, transport metadata) but includes the resolved scope, reference point, completeness code and truncation state.
patch_rules: Query-scope profiles, saved queries and closed-world scope declarations are versioned documents; every change creates a new version and preserves the prior version so previously issued results stay interpretable.

Issued result artifacts are immutable. A correction is a new issue that references and supersedes the earlier one; in-place edits of a result, its completeness declaration or its exclusion notice are prohibited.
A patch may add an optional filter, a new coded value or a new disclosure field; it may not silently change a default direction, default path mode, default scope or the meaning of an empty result.
Patches to alignment mappings record the mapping version and the conflicts they resolve or leave open, rather than asserting equivalence between code systems that are not one-to-one.
compatibility_rules: Additive changes (new optional filters, new stop-reason or truncation codes, richer disclosure) are minor and must be safely ignorable only if ignoring them cannot make a result look more complete than it is.
Any change to default scope, default direction, default path mode, ordering, completeness semantics or empty-result meaning is breaking and requires a new contract version and a migration note.
A consumer that does not understand a returned completeness code, world-scope mode or truncation state must treat the result as incomplete rather than as complete.
Projections onto a specific dialect or interface must declare which contract features they cannot honour; an unhonoured feature is a rejected request, not a silently degraded one.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the queried subject, assertion, snapshot or query result, used whenever the master system issues one
Governed global identifier or IRI from a registered namespace, used when no master-system identifier exists for the object
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting authority and the scope and reference point it is bound to
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with whole seconds present (fractional seconds permitted) and an explicit numeric offset or Z; a local time without an offset is invalid and must be rejected rather than assumed to be UTC. Event time (the period during which a dependency held, or the instant a change occurred) is recorded separately from observation time (when an assertor or external assessor observed it) and from ingestion or assertion-recording time (when it entered the store), and separately again from result issue time; an as-of read states which of these axes it binds, and a source that cannot distinguish them must have its axis recorded as unknown rather than defaulted to event time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (assertion result sets, as-of binding records, neighborhood projections, path results, comparison reports, scenario impact results, completeness declarations, page continuations and exclusion notices) are named <artifact-type>-<resolved-scope-id>-<reference-point-id>-<monotonic-sequence>. The sequence is monotonic per artifact type within a scope, contains no date or time component, and a re-issue increments the sequence and links to the superseded issue instead of overwriting it.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every issued artifact carries a content digest computed over its canonical form together with the resolved scope, bound reference point, completeness code, world-scope mode and truncation state, so that a result cannot be quoted apart from the qualifications that make it meaningful. If any of those inputs is unavailable, the artifact is issued with completeness no-assertion rather than as a verified complete result. Digest verification is a consumer-side or audit-owner activity; this model defines the digest inputs but owns neither the verification process nor the audit trail that records it.

policies: A result may be presented as evidence of independence only when it carries a declared closed-world scope, a completeness code of complete for that scope, and a truncation state of none; in every other case the strongest permitted statement is that nothing was found within the declared scope at the bound reference point.

Derived results (inferred paths, comparisons and scenario impact sets) are never written back as stored assertions by this model; they are issued as labelled, time-bound derived artifacts that reference the assertions they were computed from.
A requested filter, direction, path mode or scope that cannot be honoured is rejected explicitly; silently ignoring it is a contract violation because it changes what an empty result means.
Authorization-driven exclusions are disclosed as counts plus a decision reference and never as silent omissions; this model neither renders, re-evaluates nor enforces the underlying decision.

Reverse traversal is permitted only for edge types explicitly marked invertible; a blanket inverse operator over typed dependency edges is prohibited because dependency relations are asymmetric by construction.

Every result binds to exactly one resolved scope and one reference point; results spanning multiple reference points must be issued as separate results and combined only through an explicit comparison read.

read: Read stored assertions for a resolved endpoint at the current reference point or at a stated as-of point on a declared temporal axis.
Traverse a bounded neighborhood, or run a path query with a declared path mode and result shape, within a resolved scope at a bound reference point.
Read derived results (comparisons, scenario impact projections) and read-through references to external health indicators, each with its derivation class and freshness qualification.

Every read returns the resolved scope, bound reference point, world-scope mode, completeness code and truncation state; a read that cannot populate these fails explicitly rather than returning a bare edge list.
create: Create query-scope profiles, saved query definitions, ordering profiles and declared closed-world scope declarations, each versioned and attributed to a declaring role.
Create result artifacts as immutable issues bound to exactly one resolved scope and one reference point.
Create continuation tokens bound to one resolved scope and reference point; a token conveys position only and is never an authorization grant.
Creation of dependency assertions themselves is outside this pass; it belongs to the assertion authoring and lifecycle area of WM-XCT-037.
update: Query-scope profiles, saved queries and closed-world declarations are updated by issuing a new version while retaining prior versions, so past results remain reproducible and auditable.
Issued result artifacts, their completeness declarations and their exclusion notices are immutable; a correction is a new issue that references and supersedes the earlier one.
Re-running a saved query always produces a new result artifact and never updates an existing one.
A closed-world scope declaration may be suspended or withdrawn prospectively; withdrawal never retroactively rewrites the declaration carried by results already issued under it.
delete: Result artifacts have a bounded retention set by the adopting Dimension; the default is to retain an artifact while its bound reference point remains retrievable and then expire it. On expiry the artifact body is deleted and a tombstone is retained carrying the result identifier, resolved scope reference, reference-point identifier, completeness code, truncation state and issue time, so existing citations resolve to a deleted-but-known result rather than to nothing.
Continuation tokens are deleted at expiry; presenting an expired token returns an explicit expiry error and never silently continues against a different reference point or snapshot.

Deletion of the underlying dependency assertions is outside this model's boundary and is executed by the assertion authoring and lifecycle area of WM-XCT-037; deletion of audit and access-log entries about these reads is executed by the adopting Dimension's audit and records-retention models. This model may record only that a referenced object is no longer retrievable.

Deletion or expiry never rewrites a previously issued completeness declaration or exclusion notice; when source data is removed, later reads report a shorter retained horizon or a lower completeness code instead of retroactively altering past results.

Where a subject-rights erasure or legal-hold instruction reaches this package, execution is owned by the adopting Dimension's records-retention and privacy policy; this model contributes only the tombstone shape and the disclosure that a formerly retrievable result is gone.

roles.name: Query contract owner
responsibilities: Publish and version the query-operation contract, including default direction, default path mode, default ordering and default scope
Approve or refuse breaking changes and issue migration notes
Maintain the register of external referenced targets and confirm that none of their semantics has been absorbed locally

roles.name: Scope steward
responsibilities: Declare closed-world scopes, record the evidence supporting a complete claim, and set their validity periods
Suspend a declaration when an in-scope partition becomes unreachable or is removed
Review negative findings recorded as durable claims and set their re-verification triggers

roles.name: Reference-point custodian
responsibilities: Maintain the catalogue of retrievable reference points and publish the retained horizon
Ensure as-of resolution rules are applied consistently and that out-of-horizon requests fail explicitly
Coordinate with the storage owner on reference-point retention without assuming ownership of deletion execution

roles.name: Consuming agent or analyst
responsibilities: Bind every read to a stated scope and reference point and carry those qualifications into any downstream statement
Honour completeness codes, truncation states and exclusion notices, and refuse to infer independence from an empty open-world result
Re-run rather than reuse derived results whose validity window has lapsed

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Maintain mappings between local codes and aligned external vocabularies, recording where mappings are lossy or one-way
Record conflicts between aligned specifications instead of asserting conformance
Review projections onto specific dialects and interfaces for features they silently cannot honour

access.default_rule: Read access is denied by default and granted per resolved scope by the adopting Dimension's authorization model. This package carries only the decision reference supplied by that external decision point and the resulting exclusion disclosure; it never renders, caches for reuse, re-evaluates or enforces an authorization decision.
exceptions: A caller authorized for an endpoint but not for a neighbour receives a withheld-edge count and an exclusion notice rather than the neighbour's identity, so traversal cannot be used as an identity oracle.
Closed-world scope declarations and completeness declarations are readable more widely than the edges they qualify, so consumers can judge a negative result without seeing content.
Scenario impact results may be restricted more tightly than the assertions they derive from, because the hypothesis itself can disclose planned change or known weakness.

Withheld-edge counts may themselves be suppressed where policy forbids count disclosure; in that case the exclusion notice states that exclusions occurred and that their number is undisclosed, and the completeness code cannot be complete.
Elevated incident or emergency access is granted only through the external authorization model, with the elevated decision reference carried in the result envelope.
audit_requirements: Every issued result carries a correlation reference to the audit record written by the adopting Dimension's audit model; this model neither stores nor owns the audit trail.

The resolved scope, bound reference point, world-scope mode, completeness code, truncation state and withheld-edge disclosure are the minimum fields that must be available to the external audit record.
Authorization decision references carried in exclusion notices must be resolvable by the audit owner without exposing withheld edge content.
Issue and supersession of result artifacts, and expiry of continuation tokens, must be observable by the audit owner through the correlation reference alone.

required_fields: External referenced targets URL (authorization decision point, audit target, propagation rule model, health assessors)
read_order: AGENTS.md, to obtain the model identity, type and the URLs below
Specification URL, for scope, boundaries and the out-of-scope statements that prevent an agent from assuming ownership of engine, authorization, audit or monitoring semantics
Processes URL, for the read operations and the mandatory completeness, truncation and exclusion disclosure rules
Interface URL, for filters, ordering, paging, continuation binding and the error contract for rejected requests
Storage type URL, for available reference points, the retained horizon and snapshot availability
Reference-point and as-of semantics URL, before issuing any as-of or comparison read
Declared closed-world scope registry URL, before making or relying on any negative statement

coverage.claim: This bounded pass gives a defensible, source-grounded query-operation contract for WM-XCT-037: current and as-of assertion reads, bounded neighborhood traversal, path queries with declared modes, comparisons, scenario impact projections and referenced health reads, each governed by a mandatory result-integrity contract covering scope, completeness, ordering, snapshot-bound continuation, truncation and exclusion disclosure. It deliberately owns no engine, authorization, audit or monitoring semantics, and it does not restate the adjacent assertion-authoring area of the same model. Structural nodes without primary support are marked as gaps below rather than presented as canonical.

checklist.notes: Endpoint resolution under a named identifier authority; separate namespaces for query-invocation, result, continuation and scope identifiers; identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed IRI, then a minted UUID or ULID. Indicator binding identity is covered by the health read. No identifier encodes a date.

Covers the lifecycle this pass owns: query-scope profiles and closed-world declarations are versioned; result artifacts are immutable issues with supersession; continuations expire. Assertion lifecycle (creation, supersession, retirement) is explicitly out of scope and referenced to the adjacent authoring area.

Directed, typed edges with preserved orientation; per-edge-type invertibility instead of a blanket inverse; explicit traversal direction; seed combination modes; path modes governing node and edge repetition. Grounded in SPDX from/to, CycloneDX dependsOn/provides and SPARQL path operators.

As-of reads name their axis; requested versus resolved instants are disclosed; retained horizon and out-of-horizon errors are explicit; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated; event time, observation time, ingestion time and result issue time are kept separate.

Per-edge derivation class and provenance references; PROV-aligned attribution and derivation for computed results; assessor, method version and observation time carried for referenced indicators; propagation rule-set version recorded for scenario results.

Owner package requirements, five named roles, and explicit external owners for the decision point, audit target, rule model, health assessors and assertion lifecycle. Every referenced target names who owns execution.

Comparability testing before any comparison; rejection rather than silent dropping of unsupported filters; refusal to page without a total order; requirement that unknown completeness or truncation codes be treated as incomplete; requirement that missing integrity fields downgrade a result to no-assertion.

Deny-by-default with per-scope grants from the external decision point; exclusion disclosure by count plus decision reference; neighbour-as-oracle exception; tighter restriction of scenario results; suppression path where count disclosure itself is forbidden. Evaluation and enforcement remain at the PDP and PEP.

Result artifacts have bounded retention with a tombstone retaining identifier, scope, reference point, completeness code and issue time; continuation tokens expire with an explicit error. Execution of assertion deletion, audit-log deletion and erasure or legal-hold instructions is owned externally and named as such.

Alignments to SPARQL 1.1, GQL path modes, SPDX RelationshipCompleteness, CycloneDX compositions aggregate, OGC API - Features counts and paging, RFC 8288 link relations, RFC 7089 as-of negotiation and CSAF referenced statuses, all as alignments with recorded conflicts rather than conformance claims.

Open-world default derived from the monotonicity requirement in RDF 1.1 Semantics; independence claims permitted only under a declared, evidenced, complete and untruncated closed-world scope with a re-verification trigger.

Mandatory completeness code aligned to SPDX, partition-qualified variants aligned to CycloneDX, truncation states distinguishing page boundary from budget and scope cuts, unavailable-source references, and the rule that a missing count never implies zero or completeness.

No consulted normative source guarantees snapshot isolation for paged graph reads: OGC API - Features and RFC 8288 are silent, and AIP-158 explicitly declines to guarantee cross-page consistency. This model requires continuation tokens bound to one scope and reference point and an explicit error when that point is no longer retrievable, but the strength of the underlying guarantee depends on the storage engine and is not claimed here.
