Impact results carry qualifiers (reachable-by-rule, conditional, shielded, indeterminate) but no severity, criticality or business-value score. No defensible normative source was found for a general ranking scheme, and scoring would import risk-model semantics this pass excludes.

Dependency and impact reads in this pass are graph-topological rather than geospatial. Where an adopting Dimension has location-bearing endpoints, spatial filtering is a host-model concern applied before scope resolution.

Traversal-as-oracle risk addressed by count-only exclusion disclosure; continuation tokens are opaque, non-parseable and grant no authorization; scenario hypotheses are treated as potentially sensitive; digest inputs bind a result to its qualifications so it cannot be quoted stripped of them.

known_omissions: Concrete wire syntax and dialect bindings (SPARQL, GQL, SQL/PGQ, GraphQL, REST, MCP tool shapes) are deliberately absent; they are projections of this contract.
Query cost models, planning, caching, timeout tuning and index design.
The dependency edge-type taxonomy itself, which belongs to the adjacent assertion authoring area of WM-XCT-037.
Federated cross-organization query trust, result merging and conflict resolution beyond declaring unreachable partitions.
Subscriptions, change feeds and streaming or push-based dependency reads.
Numeric criticality, severity or blast-radius scoring for ranking impact results.
Natural-language or agent-facing query formulation and intent parsing.
Sampling and approximate-answer contracts, which would need their own error-bound disclosure semantics.
conflicts: SPARQL 1.1 arbitrary-length path matching deliberately reports connectivity without enumerating or counting paths, while GQL supplies explicit path modes and path finding that return paths. The same natural-language question therefore yields different results across engines, so this model requires the result shape and path mode to be declared rather than inferred.

SPDX RelationshipCompleteness (complete, incomplete, noAssertion) and CycloneDX compositions aggregate (ten values including first-party and third-party, proprietary and open-source partitions, plus unknown and not_specified) are not one-to-one; mapping CycloneDX to SPDX loses partition detail and conflates unknown with noAssertion. Mappings must be recorded as lossy.

CSAF v2.0 does not define the meaning of a product absent from every status group, so consumers cannot treat silence as either not-affected or no-assertion on the standard's authority. This model resolves the ambiguity locally by treating absence as no assertion and says so explicitly.

RFC 7089 negotiates prior states using RFC 1123 HTTP-date in headers, whereas this model requires RFC 3339 with an explicit offset for stored time values. A projection must convert, and must not present the best-match datetime as the datetime that was requested.

AIP-158 is design guidance rather than a standard and gives no cross-page consistency guarantee, while OGC API - Features permits omitting the matched count. Neither supplies snapshot isolation, so this model's reference-point binding is a local requirement and not an inherited one.

RDF 1.1 Semantics mandates monotonic entailment, which forbids reading absence as negation, yet SBOM practice routinely treats a delivered dependency list as exhaustive. This model sides with the standard and requires an explicit closed-world declaration before any independence claim.
regional_assumptions: No jurisdiction-specific legal requirement is assumed. Retention horizons for result artifacts, tombstone content and audit correlation are set by the adopting Dimension's jurisdictional policy, and this model states only the shape those obligations attach to.

Disclosure of withheld-edge counts may itself be restricted in some sectors or jurisdictions; the exclusion notice is deliberately designed so that count disclosure can be suppressed while still signalling that exclusions occurred.
No UTC-only operating assumption is made: every time value carries an explicit offset or Z, and calendars, working-time and regional change-freeze conventions are outside this pass.

Referenced dependency-health assessors and advisory producers are predominantly English-language, open-source-ecosystem services; coverage of regional registries, proprietary estates and non-English advisory sources is uneven and must be disclosed through the unavailable-source references rather than assumed.
adversarial_checks: Tried to justify a local authorization-filtering or policy-evaluation function so that reads could enforce visibility directly. Rejected: XACML places evaluation at the PDP and enforcement at the PEP, so only a decision reference and an exclusion disclosure are carried here, and no function evaluates or re-evaluates a decision.

Tried to add an audit or query-execution log artifact to make read history self-contained. Rejected: that would take ownership of audit-trail semantics owned by the adopting Dimension's audit model; only a correlation reference and the minimum fields that record needs are specified.

Tried to make a returned empty edge set a storable independence assertion. Rejected under the monotonicity requirement of RDF 1.1 Semantics; independence is permitted only under a declared, evidenced, complete and untruncated closed-world scope, and the permitted phrasing for every other case is fixed.

Searched for a normative source mandating cursor or snapshot isolation for paged graph reads across OGC API - Features, RFC 8288 and AIP-158, and found none; recorded as an explicit checklist gap and handled by reference-point binding rather than by claiming an unsupported guarantee.

Tested whether dependency-health scoring could be computed inside this model, since deps.dev exposes Scorecard data through a dependency API. Rejected: local computation would create a second point of truth for an external assessor's result and would pull threshold, verdict and alerting semantics into a model whose boundary excludes monitoring.

Tested whether a single generic inverse operator could satisfy direction reversal. Rejected: SPDX from/to and CycloneDX dependsOn versus provides show that dependency edge types are asymmetric and not uniformly invertible, so per-edge-type invertibility plus recorded traversal orientation is required, with non-invertible types disclosed as excluded.

Checked every bundle, layer, finding and function against each composition rationale for absorbed target semantics. Two candidates were moved out: a proposed traversal-budget enforcement rule became an engine-owned boundary note, and a proposed health-threshold finding became the inline-only referenced-indicator finding with a no-verdict question.

Considered adding path caching and materialized transitive closure to make repeat reads cheap. Rejected: a cached closure is a stored inference that would blur the stored-versus-inferred distinction and would silently answer as-of reads from a different reference point.
